editorial_note: Canto 11 data remains under full source and translation review. The Sanskrit and English records are draft material tied to the pinned source; phrase coverage and all lexical choices still require chapter-by-chapter verification.
scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for ŚB 11.17.1–11.17.58; 52 source blocks cover all 58 numbered verses, retaining the two grouped ranges and four explicit no-commentary markers.

entries.sanskrit:
ततः सप्तदशे पृष्टे स्व-धर्मे भक्ति-लक्षणे ।

हंसोक्तं धर्मम् अन्व् आह ब्रह्मचारि-गृहस्थयोः ॥

कर्माहं विद्धि सात्वताम् \[भा।पु। ११.१६.३२\] इत्य् अत्र भक्त्या कृतं कर्म मोक्ष-साधनं मद्-विभूतिर् इत्य् उक्तम्, भक्ति-साधनत्वं च कर्मणां, मयोदितेष्व् अवहितः स्व-धर्मेषु \[भा।पु। ११.१०.१\] इत्य्-आदिना, तत्र तत्रोक्तम्, न च कर्मानुष्ठातॄणां नियमेन भक्तिर् दृश्यते । अतः पृच्छति---यस् त्वयेति सप्तभिः । पूर्वं कल्पादौ त्वद्-भक्ति-लक्षणस् तत्-प्रापकस् तत्-साधनम् इत्य् अर्थः । वर्णाश्रम-हीनानाम् अपि द्वि-पदां नराणाम् । यथा येन प्रकारेणानुष्ठीयमानेन स्व-धर्मेण ॥१॥
entries.literal_english: Because Uddhava asks in the seventeenth chapter about one's own duty as the means of devotion, Śrīdhara explains that the Lord now teaches the dharma spoken by Haṁsa for brahmacārins and householders. Earlier, action performed with devotion was taught as a means to liberation and duties as means of devotion; yet devotion is not invariably seen in every performer of ritual action. Therefore Uddhava asks how the Lord's bhakti-marked duty is to be practiced by all people, even those outside the varṇāśrama system.

entries.sanskrit: ननु सम्प्रदायाद् एव ज्ञास्यते किं पुनर् वर्णनेन ? तत्राह---पुरेति । परमकं परमश् चासौ कं सुख-स्वरूपश् च तम् । यत् यम् । हंस-रूपेण धर्मोऽप्य् उक्त एव, न तु योग-मात्रम्, जानीतम् आगतं यज्ञं युष्मद् धर्म-विवक्षया\[भा।पु। ११.१३.३८\] इत्य् उक्तत्वात्। प्राग्-अनुशासितोऽपि न भविता न भविष्यति । अत्र हेतुम् आह---वक्तेति द्वाभ्याम् । ते त्वत्तोऽन्यः। कला वेदाद्यः । तत् तस्मान् नोऽस्माकं मनुष्याणां मध्ये यस्य यथा विधीयते ॥३-७॥
word_for_word: the Vedas and other branches of knowledge
entries.literal_english: Uddhava anticipates that the teaching might be known simply through the disciplic tradition. He replies that the supreme, bliss-giving dharma was indeed spoken by the Lord in the form of Haṁsa, not merely a yoga technique. Although it was taught before, it is now almost absent from the human world. No one other than Kṛṣṇa can teach, practice, or preserve it, even in Brahmā's assembly, where the personified branches of knowledge are present. Therefore Uddhava asks the Lord to describe for each person the duty characterized by devotion.

entries.sanskrit: न कतमेनापि व्याख्यातम् ।
entries.literal_english: No Śrīdhara commentary is supplied for this verse in the pinned source; the source explicitly says that it was not explained by anyone.
entries.note: The pinned source explicitly marks this verse as having no Śrīdhara commentary; the sentinel is preserved without inventing a gloss.

entries.sanskrit: धर्म्यो धर्माद् अनपेतः । कुतः ? नैःश्रेयस-करो भक्ति-जनकः । अतो मे मत्तस् तं धर्मं निबोध ॥९॥
entries.literal_english: The Lord says that Uddhava's question is righteous because it does not depart from dharma and because its answer produces the highest good by giving rise to devotion. He tells Uddhava to understand this dharma directly from Him.

entries.sanskrit: तत्रादौ मद्-उपासना-लक्षण एव मुख्यो धर्म आसीत् । आचार-लक्षणस् तु पश्चात् प्रवृत्तः । स चैवम् अनुष्ठितो भक्ति-हेतुर् इति वर्णयितुम् आह---आदाव् इति । कल्पादौ यत् कृत-युगं तस्मिन् । ते च तदा माम् उपासत एव केवलं नान्यत् कुर्वन्तीति वक्तुं कृत-युग-नाम-निरुक्तम् आह---कृत-कृत्या इति । जात्या जन्मनैव ॥१०॥
entries.literal_english: In the beginning, the principal dharma was simply worship of the Lord; duties defined by social conduct arose later. The Lord explains this to show that properly performed conduct becomes a cause of devotion. In the primordial Satya-yuga, people worshiped Him alone and did nothing else, so the age is called Kṛta: their purposes were fulfilled by birth itself.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, विधायकाभावाद् अपि तदानीं नान्यत् कर्मास्तीत्य् आह---वेद इति । धर्मश् च मनो-विषयोऽहम् एव वृष-रूप-धृक् चतुष्-पान् न क्रिया-विशेषो यज्ञादिः । अतस् तपो-निष्ठाः, मनसश् चेन्द्रियाणां च स्वैकाग्र्यं परमं तपः इति वचनाद् एकाग्रतया हंसं शुद्धं मां ध्यायन्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥११॥
word_for_word: bearing the form of a four-footed bull
entries.literal_english: Because there was no separate injunction requiring other action at that time, the Veda itself was only the syllable Om. Dharma was the Lord alone, bearing the form of a four-footed bull; it was not a particular ritual such as a sacrifice. The people were fixed in austerity, meaning the one-pointed concentration of mind and senses, and meditated on the pure Lord as Haṁsa.

entries.sanskrit: पश्चात् त्रेता-युग-प्रवेशे मे वैराज-रूपस्य प्राणान् निमित्तात् । हृदयात् सकाशात् । तस्यास् त्रय्याः सकाशात् हौत्राध्वर्य-वौद्गात्रैस् त्रि-वृत् त्रि-रूपः । यज्ञो वै विष्णुः इति श्रुतेः॥१२॥
entries.literal_english: When Tretā-yuga began, the threefold Vedic knowledge appeared from the heart of the Lord in His Virāṭ form. From that threefold Veda arose the threefold sacrifice, performed through the hotṛ, adhvaryu, and udgātṛ priests. Since scripture says that sacrifice is Viṣṇu, the sacrifice is the Lord's own manifestation.

entries.sanskrit: वर्णानाम् आश्रमाणां च धर्मान् वक्तुं तेषाम् उत्पत्तिम् आह---विप्रेति द्वभ्याम्। आत्माचारः स्व-धर्म एव लक्षणं ज्ञापको येषां ते ॥१३॥
entries.literal_english: To explain the duties of the social classes and life stages, Śrīdhara first explains their origin. The brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra arose from the mouth, arms, thighs, and feet of the cosmic Person. They are recognized by the conduct proper to their own position.

entries.sanskrit:
मम् वैराज-रूपस्य हृदो वक्षसोऽधस्तात् । ब्रह्म-चर्यम् इति नैष्ठिकाभिप्रायम्[^८७] ॥१४॥

[^८७]: नैष्ठिकाभिप्रायम् इति विचारणीयम् । अत्र
    सिद्धान्त-प्रदीपे---ब्रह्मचर्यं हृदः वक्षसः अधस्तात्
    उपकुर्वाणस्य गृहस्थावरत्वं, नैष्ठिकस्य तु सर्वथा
    ग्राम्य-सुख-परित्यागित्वेन सर्व-श्रेष्ठत्वम् । अतो ब्रह्मचर्यस
    द्वैविध्यान् मध्यस्थान्ते तद्-उत्पत्तिर् इत्य् उक्तैव । ब्रह्मचर्यस्य
    द्वैविध्यम् अग्रे २२-श्लोके प्रतिपादितम् ॥
entries.literal_english: The four āśramas are described as arising from the Lord's cosmic body: household life from the lower region, brahmacarya from the heart, forest residence from the chest, and sannyāsa from the head. Śrīdhara notes that the brahmacarya reference particularly concerns the firm, lifelong observance of the vow.

entries.sanskrit:
तेषाम् अधिकारि-विशेषेण स्वभावान् आह---वर्णानाम् इति पञ्चभिः । जन्म-स्थानानुसारिण्यः[^८८] । नीचैर्[^८९] इत्य् अव्ययम् । अतोऽयम् अर्थः, मन्दाभिर् जन्म-भूमिभिर् मन्दाः । उत्तमाभिर् उत्तमाश् चेति ॥१५॥

[^८८]: जन्म-स्थानानि मुखादीनीति भावः ॥


[^८९]: नीचैः पादादि-स्थानैर् नीचाः उत्तमैर् मुखादि-स्थानैर् उत्तमाः ।
    ताश् च ताश् चेति कर्मधारयः । वर्णानाम् आश्रमाणां च या
    जन्म-भूमयस् तद्-अनुसारिण्यो नृणां प्रकृतय आसन्न् इत्य् अन्वयः ॥
entries.literal_english: The natures of people in the varṇas and āśramas correspond to their respective places of origin in the cosmic Person. The lower locations yield lower designations and the higher locations higher ones; thus the feet and mouth illustrate the lower and higher ends of this ordering.

entries.sanskrit: तप आलोचनम् ॥१६॥
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara briefly clarifies that tapas means thoughtful examination or reflection. The listed qualities—tranquility, control, purity, contentment, patience, straightforwardness, devotion, compassion, and truth—are the nature of a brāhmaṇa.

entries.sanskrit: तेजः प्रतापः ॥१७॥
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara glosses tejas as pratāpa, or personal splendor and authority. Together with strength, steadiness, courage, endurance, generosity, initiative, firmness, reverence for brāhmaṇas, and sovereignty, it describes the kṣatriya nature.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.literal_english: No Śrīdhara commentary is supplied for this verse in the pinned source; it is marked as not explained.
entries.note: The pinned source explicitly marks this verse as having no Śrīdhara commentary; the sentinel is preserved without inventing a gloss.

entries.sanskrit: एतैर् एवाश्रम-स्वभावा अपि ज्ञेयाः ॥१९॥
entries.literal_english: The same qualities just listed are also to be used for understanding the characteristic natures of the āśramas.

entries.sanskrit:
तद्-बाह्यानां[^९०] स्वभावान् आह---अशौचम् इति । शुष्क-विग्रहो निर्मूल-कलहः । तर्षस् तृष्णा ॥२०॥

[^९०]: तद्-बाह्यानां वर्णाश्रम-धर्म-बहिष्कृतानाम् ॥
entries.literal_english: The Lord next describes those excluded from varṇāśrama duties. Their nature is marked by impurity, falsehood, theft, lack of faith, and dry or groundless quarrelsomeness; tṛṣṇā here means craving or thirst.

entries.sanskrit:
तत्र तावत् सर्व-साधारणं धर्मम् आह---अहिंसेति । वर्ण-ग्रहणम् उपलक्षणार्थम्[^९१] । वर्ण-धर्मान् गृहस्थ-प्रकरणे वक्ष्यति ॥२१॥

[^९१]: उपलक्षणार्थम् आश्रम-धर्मत्व-ज्ञापनार्थम् ॥
word_for_word: acting for the affection and welfare of beings
entries.literal_english: This verse gives the dharma common to everyone: nonviolence, truth, non-stealing, freedom from lust, anger, and greed, and activity intended to please and benefit living beings. The word varṇa is inclusive here and also indicates that these are duties common to the āśramas; specific varṇa duties are explained later in the householder section.

entries.sanskrit: प्रथमं तावद् आश्रमेषु ब्रह्मचारिणो धर्मा वर्ण्यन्ते । स च द्विविधः, उपकुर्वाणको नैष्ठिकश् च । तत्राद्य् अस्य धर्मान् आह---द्वितीयम् इति नवभिः । द्विजस् त्रैवर्णिकः । आनुपूर्व्याद् गर्भाधानादि-संस्कार-क्रमेण द्वितीयम् उपनयनाख्यं जन्म प्राप्याचार्येणाहूतो ब्रह्म वेदम् अधीयीत । च-कारात् तद्-अर्थं च विचारयेत् ॥२२॥
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara begins the duties of the brahmacārin, who is of two kinds: the temporary student and the lifelong naiṣṭhika. The first instruction concerns the former. A dvija means one of the three higher varṇas; after the sequential rites and the second birth of upanayana, he should be called by the teacher and study the Veda, also reflecting on its meaning.

entries.sanskrit:
किं च, मेखलादीन् कुशांश् च दधत् । तत्राक्ष-शब्देनाक्ष-माला । कथं-भूतः ? जटिलः अनभ्यङ्गादिना जात-जटः । तथा अधौत-दद्-वासोऽरक्त-पीठः । दन्ताश् च वासश् च दद्-वासांसि न धौतानि तानि यस्य सः अधौत-दद्-वासाः । स चासाव् अरक्त-पीठश् च, न तु कौतुकादिना रक्तं पीठम्[^९३] आसनं यस्य सः ॥२३॥

[^९३]: सौन्दर्य-निमित्त-केश-दन्त-वस्त्र-नैर्मल्यासन-वैचित्र्य-शून्य
    इत्य् अर्थः ॥
entries.literal_english: The student should wear the belt, deerskin, staff, rosary, sacred thread, and water pot, and carry kuśa grass. Akṣa refers to a rosary. He is matted-haired from abstaining from bodily anointing, wears unwashed garments, and uses an unadorned seat—not one chosen for cosmetic or decorative appeal.

entries.sanskrit: जपश् चोच्चारो मूत्र-पुरीषोत्सर्गो जपोच्चारं तस्मिन् वाग्-यतो मौनी भवेत् ।
entries.literal_english: During bathing, eating, fire offerings, recitation, and bodily evacuation, the student should restrain his speech and remain silent as required. He should not cut the nails or hair growing in the armpits and genital region.

entries.sanskrit:
रेतो बुद्धि-पूर्वं नावकिरेन् नोत्सृजेत् । ब्रह्म-व्रत-धरो[^९६] गृहस्थः । स्वयम् एव कथञ्चिद्[^९७]अवकीर्णे अवगाह्य स्नात्वा यतासुः कृत-प्राणायामस् त्रि-पदीं गायत्रीं जपेत्॥२५॥

[^९६]: ब्रह्मचारी।


[^९७]: अवकीर्णे उत्सृष्टे सति ।
word_for_word: one who holds the brahmacarya vow
entries.literal_english: A holder of the brahmacarya vow should never intentionally emit semen. If it happens accidentally, he should bathe, perform breath control, and recite the three-footed Gāyatrī mantra.

entries.sanskrit: सन्ध्ये च द्वे यत-वाग् जपन्न् उपासीत । मध्याह्ने सन्ध्या-निमित्तं मौनं नास्तीति द्वि-वचनम् ॥२६॥
entries.literal_english: He should worship at the two sandhyās, morning and evening, while restraining his speech and reciting the mantra. Śrīdhara explains that the dual wording does not impose silence at the midday sandhyā; the instruction for silence applies to the two principal sandhyā times.

entries.sanskrit: न कतमेन व्याख्यातम्।
entries.literal_english: No Śrīdhara commentary is supplied for this verse in the pinned source; the source explicitly marks it as unexplained.
entries.note: The pinned source explicitly marks this verse as having no Śrīdhara commentary; the sentinel is preserved without inventing a gloss.

entries.sanskrit: अन्यद् अपि यत् सम्प्राप्तं तच् च निवेदयेत् । तेनानुज्ञातं तु संयतः सन्न् उपयुञ्जीतेत्य् अर्थः ॥२८॥
entries.literal_english: The student should bring his morning and evening alms and offer them to the teacher. Whatever else he obtains should also be offered. He may consume only what the teacher has permitted, and he should do so with self-control.

entries.sanskrit:
यान-शय्यासन-स्थानैः । यान्तं पृष्ठतो यानेन । निद्रितम् अप्रमत्ततया समीप-शयनेन । विश्रान्तं पाद-संवाहनादिभिः समीपासनेन । आसीनं कृताञ्जलिः । नियोग[^९९]-प्रतीक्षया नातिदूरेऽवस्थानेनेत्य् अर्थः ॥२९॥

[^९९]: आज्ञा ।
entries.literal_english: While serving the teacher, the student should remain like a humble servant. When the teacher travels, sleeps, or rests, he should attend appropriately—following behind, serving near the bed, and serving at a nearby seat. With folded hands he should wait for the teacher's instruction, without standing too far away.

entries.sanskrit: एवं-भूतं वृत्तं यस्य सः ॥३०॥
entries.literal_english: He should live in the teacher's school with this conduct, free from sensual enjoyments, maintaining the vow without interruption until his education is complete.

entries.sanskrit:
एवम् उपकुर्वाणकस्य धर्मान् उक्त्वा नैष्ठिकस्य विशेष-धर्मान् आह---यदीति षड्भिः । असौ ब्रह्मचारी यदि छन्दसां लोकं महर्-लोकं ततो ब्रह्म-लोकं चारोक्ष्यन्न्[^१००] आरोढुम् इच्छतीत्य् अर्थः । यद् वा, छन्दसां लोकम् इति ब्रह्म-लोक-विशेषणम्, यत्र मूर्ति-धराः कलाः \[भा।पु। ११.१७.५\] इत्य् उक्तत्वात् । तर्हि बृहद्-व्रतः सन् बृहन् नैष्ठिकं व्रतं यस्य सः । विन्यसेत् समर्पयेद् अधिक-स्वाध्यायार्थम् अधीत-निष्क्रयार्थं[^१०१] च ॥३१॥

[^१००]: फलितार्थ-कथनम् एतत् ।


[^१०१]: निष्क्रयार्थम् अधीतस्य वेदस्यानृण्य-रूप-दक्षिणार्थम् ॥
entries.literal_english: After describing the temporary student's duties, Śrīdhara explains the special rule for the lifelong brahmacārin. If he desires to ascend to the world of the Vedas—understood either as Maharloka and Brahmaloka or as Brahmaloka itself—he must maintain the great vow and offer his body to the teacher, both for further study and as the proper repayment for the Veda received.

entries.sanskrit: ब्रह्म-वर्चो वेदाभ्यासजं तेजस् तद्वान् ॥३२॥
word_for_word: the splendor born of Vedic study
entries.literal_english: The student should worship the Supreme Lord without seeing a difference between the sacred fire, the teacher, his own self, and all living beings. A sinless student who possesses brahma-varchas, the radiance produced by Vedic study, worships in this unified understanding.

entries.sanskrit: तस्यैव वनस्थ-यति-साधारण-धर्मान् आह---स्त्रीणाम् इति । निरीक्षणं भाव-गर्भम् । क्ष्वेलनं परिहासः । एवम् आदिकं त्यजेत् । मिथुनी-भूतान् अग्रतस् त्यजेत्, न पश्येद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३३॥
entries.literal_english: The forest-dweller and renunciant should avoid looking at women with amorous intent, touching them, conversing with them, joking with them, and similar behavior. He should avoid even seeing sexually united people directly in front of him.

entries.sanskrit: तस्यैव सर्वाश्रम-साधारणं धर्मम् आह---शौचम् इति द्वाभ्याम् ॥३४॥
entries.literal_english: The next two verses state duties common to all āśramas: purity, ācamana, bathing, worship at the sandhyās, worship of the Lord, straightforwardness, and the other disciplines listed in the verses. Śrīdhara identifies these as general āśrama duties rather than rules belonging only to one order.

entries.sanskrit: निष्काम-नैष्ठिकस्य तु मोक्षं फलम् आह---एवम् इति । अमलो निष्कामश् चेद् दग्धः कर्माशयोऽन्तः-करणं यस्य तथा-भूतः सन् मद्-भक्तो भवति ॥३६॥
word_for_word: whose store of karma is burned
entries.literal_english: For the desireless lifelong brahmacārin, the result is liberation. If he is pure and free from desire, with the store of karma in his inner instrument burned away, he becomes devoted to the Lord.

entries.sanskrit: उपकुर्वाणस्य समावर्तन-प्रकारम् आह---अथेति । अनन्तरं द्वितीयाश्रमम् आवेक्ष्यन् प्रवेष्टुम् इच्छन् यथा यथावद्-विचारित-वेदार्थः स्नायात् । अभ्यङ्गादिकं कृत्वा समावर्तेतेत्य् अर्थः ॥३७॥
word_for_word: having examined the meaning of the Veda
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara explains the completion ceremony of the temporary student. When he wishes to enter the second āśrama, after properly examining the meaning of the Veda, he should bathe—having performed the required anointing and related rites—and return from studentship.

entries.sanskrit:
तस्याधिकारानुरूपम् आश्रम-विकल्प-समुच्चयाव् आह---गृहम् इति । स-कामश् चेद् गृहम् अन्तः-करण-शुद्ध्य्-आदि-कामश् चेद् वनं प्रविशेत् । शुद्धान्तः-करणः स च द्विजोत्तमो ब्राह्मणश् चेत् प्रव्रजेद् इत्य् अर्थः । द्विजोत्तम इत्य् उक्तेः क्षत्रिय-वैश्ययोर् न प्रव्रज्याधिकार इति सूचयति । यद् वा, आश्रमाद् आश्रमान्तरं गच्छेत् । अन्यथा अनाश्रमी प्रतिलोमं[^१०४] च नाचरेद् इत्य् अर्थः । अमत्-पर इति वा छेदः । स्व-भक्तस्याश्रम-नियम-भावस्य वक्ष्यमाणत्वात् ॥३८॥

[^१०४]: अनाश्रमी न तिष्ठेत क्षणम् एकम् अपि द्विजः इति स्मृतेः ।
    प्रतिलोमं गृहं वनं वेत्य् आद्य् उक्त-व्युत्क्रमेण ॥
entries.literal_english: According to his qualification, a person may enter household life, the forest, or renunciation. One who seeks ordinary enjoyments enters the household; one who seeks purification enters the forest; and a pure-minded brāhmaṇa may renounce. Śrīdhara also reads the verse as requiring movement from one āśrama to another rather than living without an āśrama or reversing the proper order, while the devotee's own āśrama restriction is addressed later.

entries.sanskrit:
विवाह-नियम-पूर्वकं वर्ण-धर्मैः सह गृहस्थ-धर्मान् आह---गृहार्थीति। सदृशीं स-वर्णाम् । अजुगुप्सितां कुलतो लक्षणतश् चानिन्दिताम् । कामतस् तु याम् अन्याम् उद्वहेत् तां स-वर्णाम् अनु तस्या अनन्तरम् । तत्रापि वर्ण-क्रमेणोद्वहेद् इत्य् अर्थः।

> तिस्रो-वर्णानुपूर्व्येण द्वेतथैका यथा-क्रमम् । >
> ब्राह्मण-क्षत्रिय-विशां भार्याः स्वाः शूद्र-जन्मनः ॥ इति स्मृतेः > ॥३९॥
entries.literal_english: The householder should marry a suitable woman of the same varṇa, one not blameworthy by family or qualities. If desire leads him to marry another wife, he should take the next one in the prescribed varṇa sequence. Śrīdhara cites the rule that a brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, or vaiśya may have wives in the ordered sequence, including a śūdra-born wife where the rule allows.

entries.sanskrit: इज्यादयस् त्रैवर्णिकानाम् आवश्यका धर्माः । प्रतिग्रहादि-त्रयं तु वृत्तिः । सा च ब्राह्मणस्यैव ॥४०॥
entries.literal_english: Worship, study, and charity are obligatory duties for the three higher varṇas. Accepting gifts, teaching, and officiating for others are forms of livelihood belonging specifically to the brāhmaṇa.

entries.sanskrit: तत्रापि मुख्यां मुख्यतमां चान्यां वृत्तिम् आह---प्रतिग्रहम् इति । तयोर् यजनाध्यापनयोर् अपि कार्पण्यादि-दोषं पश्यन् शिलैः स्वामि-त्यक्तैः क्षेत्र-पतितैः कणिशैः ॥४१॥
word_for_word: the fault of dependence or meanness
entries.literal_english: Among the possible livelihoods, Śrīdhara points to an especially pure alternative. Seeing the faults such as dependence and meanness that may accompany officiating and teaching, the brāhmaṇa may live by gleaning grains abandoned by their owners and fallen in the field.

entries.sanskrit: एवं च वृत्ति-कार्श्यं ब्राह्मणेन सोढव्यम् इत्य् आह---ब्राह्मणस्येति ॥४२॥
entries.literal_english: The brāhmaṇa should tolerate hardship in livelihood. His body is not meant for petty pleasures; it is meant for difficult austerity in this life and for attaining unlimited happiness after death.

entries.sanskrit: उञ्छ-वृत्तिर् नाम विपण्य्-आदि-पतित-कणोपादानं तां शिल-वृत्त्य्-ऐकी-कृत्य तया तुष्ट-चित्तस्य मोक्षं फलम् आह---शिलोञ्छेति । महान्तम् आतिथ्यादि-लक्षणम् । विरजं निष्कामम् । जुषाणः सेवमानः । गृह एव गृहस्थाश्रम एव । नाति-प्रसक्तोऽति-शयेन रागम् अकुर्वन् । शान्तिम् उपैति मोक्षाधिकारी भवति ॥४३॥
entries.literal_english: Uñcha-vṛtti means gathering grains fallen in the marketplace and similar places; combined with śila-vṛtti, gleaning in fields, it can sustain a contented person. By practicing this great, desireless dharma—marked by hospitality and related duties—while remaining in the house without excessive attachment, the brāhmaṇa attains peace and becomes qualified for liberation.

entries.sanskrit: एवम् अधनस्य महत्-फलम् उक्त्वा सधनानाम् अप्य् आह त्रिभिः । समुद्धरन्ति दारिद्र्याद् उत्तारयन्ति । विप्रम् इत्य् उपलक्षणम् । मत्-परायणं यं कम् अपि॥४४॥
entries.literal_english: After describing the great result available to a poor brāhmaṇa, the Lord speaks for three verses about those who possess wealth. Those who rescue a distressed, God-devoted brāhmaṇa from poverty—brāhmaṇa being used as an inclusive designation for a devoted person—will themselves be rescued from danger like people carried across an ocean by a boat.

entries.sanskrit: राज्ञस् त्व् आवश्यकम् एतद् इत्य् आह---सर्वा इति ॥४५॥
entries.literal_english: This duty is especially necessary for a king: he should rescue all his subjects from distress as a father does, and should steady and protect himself by his own discipline just as the leader of elephants controls the elephants.

entries.sanskrit: न कतमेनापि व्याख्यातम् ।
entries.literal_english: No Śrīdhara commentary is supplied for this verse in the pinned source; it is explicitly marked as not explained.
entries.note: The pinned source explicitly marks this verse as having no Śrīdhara commentary; the sentinel is preserved without inventing a gloss.

entries.sanskrit: सर्वेषाम् आपद्-वृत्तीर् आह---सीदन्न् इति त्रिभिः । पण्यैर् विक्रयार्हैर् न तु सुरा-लवणाद्यैः । तत्राप्य् आपदाक्रान्तश् चेत् खड्गेन क्षत्रिय-वृत्त्या वा । यद्य् अपि गौतमोऽनन्तरा पापीयसीं वृत्तिम् आतिष्ठिद् इति स्मरन् खङ्ग-धारणं पण्य-विक्रयाच् छ्रेष्ठं मन्यते तथापि हिंसातो वणिग् वृत्तिर् एव श्रेष्ठेति भगवतो मतम् । न तु श्व-वृत्त्या नीच-सेवया ॥४७॥
entries.literal_english: The Lord now gives emergency occupations for everyone. A distressed brāhmaṇa may cross the crisis by selling permissible merchandise, not intoxicants, salt, and similar prohibited goods. If still overcome by danger, he may take up the sword, a kṣatriya's work. Although another authority may rank sword-bearing above trade, the Lord considers the merchant's livelihood better because sword-bearing involves violence; serving a low master like a dog is not approved.

entries.sanskrit: तत्राप्य् आपदि मृगयया । विप्र-रूपेण वा अध्यापनादिना ॥४८॥
word_for_word: in the guise of a brāhmaṇa
entries.literal_english: In distress, a kṣatriya may live by a vaiśya's livelihood or by hunting. He may also act in the guise of a brāhmaṇa, for example by teaching, but should never adopt the degrading livelihood of a dog-like servant.

entries.sanskrit: कारवः प्रतिलोम-ज-विशेषा बुरुडादयस् तेषां वृत्तिं कटादि-क्रियाम् । आपद्-उत्तीर्णस् तु नानुकल्पेन वर्तेतेत्य् आह---कृच्छ्राद् इति ॥४९॥
entries.literal_english: A vaiśya in distress may adopt the śūdra's occupation, and a śūdra may perform the work of artisans such as making mats. The term kāru refers to artisan groups born from mixed unions. Once the crisis has passed, a person should not continue living by an emergency substitute occupation.

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं वृत्ति-व्यवस्थाम् उक्त्वा पुनर् गृहस्थस्यावश्यकान् पञ्च-यज्ञान् आह---वेदाध्ययनं ब्रह्म-यज्ञस् तेन ऋषीन् स्वधा-कारेण पितॄन् स्वाहा-कारेण देवान् बलि-हरणेन भूतानि अन्नाद्यैर् अन्नोदकादिभिर् मनुष्यान् इति ज्ञातव्यम् । यथोदयं विभवानुसारतः । तेष्व् ईश्वर-दृष्टिं विधत्ते, मद्-रूपाणीति ॥५०॥
entries.literal_english: After regulating livelihood, the Lord lists the five daily sacrifices required of a householder. Vedic study is the sacrifice to the sages; svadhā is offered to the ancestors; svāhā to the gods; bali offerings to living beings; and food and water to human beings. These are to be performed according to one's means, seeing all their recipients as forms of the Lord.

entries.sanskrit: आवश्यकं धर्मम् उक्त्वा शक्त्य्-अनुसारं धर्मम् आह---यदृच्छया उद्यमं विना । उपार्जितेन वा शुक्लेन स्व-वृत्त्या लब्धेन शुद्धेन वा धनेन भृत्यान् पोष्यान् ॥५१॥
word_for_word: by what comes of its own accord
entries.literal_english: After stating necessary duties, the Lord describes duties according to ability. With wealth that comes without deliberate exertion, or with pure wealth earned through one's own proper occupation, a person should support dependents without oppressing them and should perform sacrifices according to justice.

entries.sanskrit: गृहस्थस्यापि निवृत्ति-निष्ठाम् एवाह---कुटुम्बेष्व् इति त्रिभिः । न प्रमाद्येद् ईश्वर-निष्ठायां प्रमत्तो न भवेत् । ननु दृष्टादृष्टार्थ-कर्मासक्तस्य कथम् अप्रमादो विचारेण ? इत्य् आह---विपश्चिद् इति ॥५२॥
entries.literal_english: Even a householder should maintain a disposition toward withdrawal: he should not become attached to family members or negligent in devotion to the Lord. If one asks how a person involved in duties for visible and invisible results can remain alert, Śrīdhara answers that the wise person sees the unseen future results as perishable just like visible things.

entries.sanskrit: तत्रापि दृष्टेष्व् आसक्तेर् अधिकत्वात् तेषां नश्वरतां प्रपञ्चयति, पुत्रादीनाम् एकत्र सङ्गमः पान्थानां प्रपायां सङ्गम इव । तत्र हेतुः, अनु-देहं प्रतिहम् एते वियन्ति नश्यन्ति निद्रानुवर्ती स्वप्नो निद्रापाये यथेति ॥५३॥
entries.literal_english: Because attachment to visible family is especially strong, the Lord explains its impermanence. The meeting of sons, wife, and relatives is like travelers meeting at a watering place. With each body these relationships pass away, just as a dream dependent on sleep disappears when sleep ends.

entries.sanskrit: अतिथिवद् उदासीनः ॥५४॥
entries.literal_english: Reflecting in this way, a person becomes free. He should live in the household like a guest—detached, without possessiveness or egoism—and should not allow the houses and possessions to bind him.

entries.sanskrit: अस्याप्य् आश्रम-विकल्पम् आह---कर्मभिर् इति । गृहाश्रम एव तिष्ठेत् । यदि प्रजावांस् तर्हि प्रव्रजेद् वा ॥५५॥
entries.literal_english: Even such a devotee has a choice of āśrama. He may remain in household life after worshiping the Lord through the duties of the householder; if he has children and the relevant responsibilities are fulfilled, he may instead renounce and become a mendicant.

entries.sanskrit: गृहाद्य्-आसङ्गे दोषम् आह---यस् त्व् इति त्रिभिः ।
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara introduces the next three verses as a description of the fault in attachment to home and related objects.

entries.sanskrit: बन्धम् एवाभिनयेन दर्शयति---अहो इति । बाला आत्मजा यस्याः सा, आत्म-जाश् च मां विना अनाथाः सन्तः कथं जीविष्यन्तीति ॥५७॥
entries.literal_english: The bondage is shown through the person's own anxious speech: 'Alas, my parents are old, my wife has a young child, and my children are helpless without me—how will these suffering dependents live?'

entries.sanskrit: गृहे य आशयो वासना तेन आ सर्वतः क्षिप्तं हृदयं यस्य सः । अन्धं तमोऽति-तामसीं योनिम् ।
entries.literal_english: The heart of the foolish person is completely seized by the latent desire for home. Still unsatisfied, he continually thinks of those dependents; after death he enters blind darkness, meaning an intensely tamasic form of existence.
